extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, peer reviewers, and journal staff of medical journals
extracted.subtask_description: ICMJE Recommendations outlining roles, responsibilities, ethical standards, and technical requirements for conducting, reporting, editing, and publishing scholarly work in medical journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the aims and scope of the ICMJE Recommendations as guidance for conduct, reporting, editing, and publication of scholarly work in medical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed explanatory text not present on this page; full Recommendations contain specific aims and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Should Use the Recommendations?
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies the intended users of the Recommendations (e.g., authors, editors, peer reviewers, publishers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed guidance not present on this page; full Recommendations list target audiences and applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: History of the Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides background and development history of the ICMJE Recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical context referenced; detailed history not present on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining the Role of Authors and Contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for who qualifies as an author or contributor and how roles/contributions should be defined and declared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full criteria and examples (e.g., authorship criteria, contributorship statements) are in the Recommendations; not detailed on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Financial and Non-Financial Relationships and Activities, and Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for declaring financial and non-financial relationships, activities, and potential conflicts of interest by authors and contributors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed disclosure expectations and formats (e.g., forms, examples) are in the full Recommendations; not detailed on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities in the Submission and Peer-Review Process
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibilities of authors, reviewers, and editors during submission and peer review (e.g., accuracy, confidentiality, timeliness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific responsibilities and recommended practices are in the full Recommendations; not included here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Owners and Editorial Freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards regarding independence of editorial decision-making and relationships between journal owners/publishers and editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed policies to protect editorial freedom are in the full Recommendations; not included on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Research Participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for ethical protection of human and animal research participants, including informed consent and IRB/ethics approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific obligations, documentation, and reporting requirements are provided in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections and Version Control
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies for issuing corrections, retractions, and maintaining version control of published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures and examples for errata, corrigenda, retractions, and versioning are detailed in the full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and handling of scientific misconduct such as fabrication, falsification, and plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigation processes, responsibilities, and reporting actions are provided in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on copyright ownership, licenses, and permissions related to published material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific policies and recommended practices (e.g., author rights, transfer, open licensing) are in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for handling redundant, duplicate, or overlapping publications, including disclosure and citation of related work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions and remediation steps for overlapping publication cases are detailed in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on publishing correspondence (letters to the editor, responses) and appropriate handling of post-publication discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance for correspondence handling is included in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on fees related to publication (e.g., article processing charges) and transparency about costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details on fee disclosure and handling are in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplements, Theme Issues, and Special Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for publishing supplements, themed issues, or special series, including sponsorship and content control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific requirements for disclosure, editorial control, and labeling of such content are in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsorships and Partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on relationships with sponsors and partners and the effects on editorial independence and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations for disclosure and preservation of editorial freedom in sponsored content are detailed in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and best practices for electronic publication (online content, archiving, metadata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical and ethical recommendations for electronic publishing are provided in full text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing advertising in medical journals and separation from editorial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on disclosure, labeling, and maintaining editorial independence from advertisers is available in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journals and the Media
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on interactions between journals/authors and the media, including press releases and public communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practices for accurate media communication are detailed in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards related to clinical trial reporting, registration, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirements for trial registration and reporting standards; full details are in the Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing a Manuscript for Submission to a Medical Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on manuscript structure, reporting standards, and preparation prior to submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific formatting, reporting checklists (e.g., CONSORT), and technical instructions are in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sending the Manuscript to the Journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and requirements for submitting manuscripts, including required statements and submission materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission checklists and required documentation (e.g., conflict disclosures, author contributions) are in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and expectations for authors' use of artificial intelligence tools in preparing manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed rules about disclosure, attribution, and permissible use of AI are provided in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI by Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on reviewers' use of AI tools during peer review and associated confidentiality/ethical considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific expectations and limitations for reviewer AI use are in the full Recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' Role in Ensuring Responsible Use of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors' responsibilities to set policies and oversee appropriate use of AI in authorship and peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance for editors on AI policy-setting and enforcement is provided in the full Recommendations.
